clue.text: Navigator breaking record crossing Roman square

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart and its pieces end up in a new order
the shuffled letters lie across the other piece, so one sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
four, a square number, in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A rally navigator smashing a lap record while driving across an old Roman piazza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' points to a number that is a perfect square, written the Roman way, not to a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-driver in rallying sits beside the driver and reads the pace notes, acting as navigator.

clue.text: Flippin’ Young Conservative animals in The Swan

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: YC is the abbreviation for a Young Conservative
gnus are African antelopes

explanation.surface: An exasperated young Tory complains about the animals in a pub called The Swan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flippin'' reads as a mild curse but signals the turnaround. The Young Conservatives are the youth wing of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Cygnus is the northern constellation whose Latin name means the Swan.

clue.text: Destroy Chester, say

blocks.note: Deva was the Roman name for Chester
to state is to say

explanation.surface: An order to wipe out the English city of Chester, as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like it marks Chester as an example, but it is the verb to state. Chester is a walled city in north-west England, founded as a Roman fort.
explanation.definitionFit: To devastate is to destroy utterly, laying waste to a place.

clue.text: Lollard queen mounted by Eric?

blocks.note: Eric Idle of the Monty Python comedy team
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A medieval heretic monarch with a man named Eric on top of her.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, being mounted by means having the other piece above, so IDLE comes first. Lollard is an old word for a lazy loafer as well as the religious follower.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollard, in an archaic sense, is a lounger or idle person, a near synonym of loafer.

clue.text: Take in a means to worry

blocks.note: to take in food is to eat it
taken as written
a means of doing something is a way

explanation.surface: Absorbing a method for fretting.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat away at someone is to worry or gnaw at them persistently.

clue.text: Rhode Island blocks special award for writer

indicators.note: a thing that blocks sits in the middle of the way, so these letters go in the middle of the other piece

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for special
Commander of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
the postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: A state official stands in the way of an honour being given to an author.
explanation.walkthrough: The award is a British honour given by the monarch; 'blocks' puts the state inside it, not in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a writer, especially one who copied documents by hand before printing.

clue.text: Wacky baccy free in coffee shop

indicators.note: wacky means crazy and erratic, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wacky baccy, slang for cannabis, handed out free in a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Amsterdam's cannabis-selling coffee shops; baccy is British slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A cybercafe is a café offering internet access, so it is a kind of coffee shop.

clue.text: Private decapitated evildoer

indicators.note: losing its head means the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a sinner does evil

explanation.surface: A soldier beheads a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier's rank but means personal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner feelings are private ones, kept within.

clue.text: Religious group bottles many perfumes

indicators.note: to bottle something is to shut it up inside

blocks.note: the Essenes were an ancient Jewish sect
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number

explanation.surface: A sect stores lots of scents in bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Essences are concentrated extracts of plants used as perfumes.

clue.text: Sweet refined man kisses Mr Cummings

blocks.note: a toff is a posh, well-bred man
the poet e e cummings

explanation.surface: A gentleman kisses a man called Cummings.
explanation.walkthrough: Kisses here means touches, so the two pieces sit side by side. Toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy sweet made from boiled sugar and butter.

clue.text: Hammer a bit of rock from stones

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here just the opening letter of the word that follows
taking something from a word means removing it

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
gravel is small stones

explanation.surface: Someone chipping a fragment of rock out of a heap of stones.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAVEL loses its R to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gavel is the small wooden hammer an auctioneer or judge bangs.

clue.text: Instruments of death returned by doctor

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word reads from end to start

blocks.note: mort is the French (and old English) word for death
Bones is slang for a doctor, as with the ship's doctor in Star Trek

explanation.surface: Deadly weapons handed back by a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instruments of death' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trombones are brass musical instruments with a slide.

clue.text: Open University’s up-to-date welcoming lecturers?

indicators.note: a word that welcomes another takes it inside

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
up-to-date means new
the Senior Common Room, where university lecturers gather

explanation.walkthrough: 'Open University' looks like the famous institution; Open is the definition and University gives U. SCR, the senior common room, stands for the staff in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unscrew a lid or jar is to open it by turning.

clue.text: Coded language seen in unlooked-for translation

indicators.note: letters seen in a phrase are found sitting inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A surprising translation reveals a secret code.
explanation.definitionFit: FORTRAN is an early computer programming language, used for writing code.

clue.text: Ugly person‘s outburst about drunken orgy

about means around, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: a gale of laughter is an outburst
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An unattractive man shouts in protest at a drunken party.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a grotesque carved face on a building, so by extension a very ugly person.

clue.text: One of two men maybe chants?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; Gregorian describes the chants

blocks.note: the first of the men: a man's name
the second man's name

explanation.surface: A man of a pair perhaps sings.
explanation.walkthrough: Two men's names, Gregor and Ian, run together. Gregorian chant is plainsong named after Pope Gregory I.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregorian is the name of the plainsong style of church chant, so it describes the chants.

clue.text: Christian’s love showing disbelief

blocks.note: first meaning: the Greek word for selfless Christian love
second meaning: with the mouth wide open in amazement

explanation.surface: A believer's devotion meeting a sceptic's stare.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: a-GAH-pay for the love, a-GAPE for the open mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape is New Testament Greek for brotherly love, and someone agape is open-mouthed in astonishment.

clue.text: Star graduate boards a modified lander

a passenger who boards goes inside the vehicle

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged
a Bachelor of Arts is a graduate

explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is the bright red star forming the eye of the constellation Taurus.

clue.text: Mature adult leaving with new teenagers?

a grown-up is an adult
W is the abbreviation for with
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.walkthrough: GROWNUP loses its W and N. The question mark marks teenagers as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers form one age group, a band of people of similar years.

clue.text: Joy embraces bishop in church property

blocks.note: glee is joy

clue.text: Stops Susanna acquiring pass

blocks.note: Sus. is the standard abbreviation for the apocryphal Book of Susanna

clue.text: Dictator of southern city in Estonia we hear

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
the capital of Estonia

clue.text: Strut and length of material on Mongolian tent

explanation.definitionFit: To swagger is to strut, walking with arrogant confidence.

clue.text: Artist using carbon in medium

clue.text: Attempt to refurbish an old boat

explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is the flat-bottomed boat rowed along the canals of Venice.

clue.text: Remarkable denial of 1950’s teenager? I’m ______!

clue.text: Sketching what a groundsman may be doing!
